grammar.title: 2B: Present perfect + for / since, present perfect continuous
grammar.explanation:
We use **have been, has been** (present perfect) with **for** and **since** for things that started in the past and are still true now. She has been a **kind** nurse since last year.

**For** is a period of time: for two years, for three days. **Since** is a start point: since Monday, since twenty twenty.

Ask **How long have you been proud of her?** to ask about an unfinished time.

The present perfect continuous is **have been + verb-ing**: I have been learning. We use it for actions that started in the past and are still true now. He has been **patient** since the morning.
examples: I have been *happy* for three days. (for + a period)
My friend has been *sad* since Monday. (since + a start point)
She has known her *kind* teacher since last year. (still true now)
He has been helping his *shy* friend since the morning. (action still going)
They have been smiling because they feel *proud*. (clear result now)
A *brave* boy has been waiting for one hour. (for + a period)
An *honest* man has been telling his story since five o'clock. (continuous action)
Her *friendly* smile has been changing my *mood* since we met. (two words)
